title: Can LLMs Rank the Harmfulness of Smaller LLMs? We are Not There Yet
benchmark_measurement: Detection of discriminatory language, stereotyping, and bias based on religion as part of a broader set of harm categories (including offensiveness, privacy invasion, etc.).
findings: Religion was included as a criterion for identifying harmful content, specifically under 'Discriminatory or Biased Language'. The paper's general finding is that large LLMs (GPT40, Claude3.5 Sonnet, Llama3.1-70b) show only low to moderate agreement with human ratings when asked to rank the harmfulness of outputs from smaller LLMs. This suggests that automated moderation of harmful content, including religious bias, is not yet on par with human judgment.
